{
  "ideas": [
    {
      "name": "Adaptive Aggregation Regime Selector (AARS)",
      "levels": ["organism", "community"],
      "mechanism": "Each frame is first evaluated by a lightweight Jev score (e.g., edge‑density heuristic). Based on the recent moving‑average of Jev‑validated fidelity for the current VLM critics, a controller switches between a consensus rule (pick the critic whose reconstruction agrees with the majority) and a union rule (merge all distinct object labels). The selector updates its regime after every frame using a simple reinforcement signal (Δ fidelity).",
      "jev_role": "Provides the per‑frame fidelity estimate that drives the reinforcement signal and also validates the chosen regime’s output.",
      "hypothesis": "Dynamic switching between consensus and union will raise overall fidelity on edge‑glyph text from the static consensus level 0.354 (E2) to >0.410 (≥ 0.056 improvement, 95 % CI non‑overlapping). Refuted if measured fidelity ≤0.380.",
      "builds_on": "E2 (community jury consensus advantage) and E4 (union advantage when members are weak).",
      "cost": "≈ 1 Jev query per frame for baseline score + 6 VLM critic calls per frame + 1 extra Jev query for validation; well within a single GPU hour on the current cluster.",
      "beyond_classic_ml": "Implements a meta‑controller that adaptively chooses aggregation strategy based on online performance, a form of self‑tuning ensemble beyond static bagging or voting."
    },
    {
      "name": "Self‑Organizing Perspective Specialisation (SOPS)",
      "levels": ["community", "family", "organ"],
      "mechanism": "Instantiate a set of perspective agents (brightness, edge, motion, braille, hybrid‑A, hybrid‑B). Every tissue (4×4 tile) queries each perspective’s local Jev‑score on its patch. Perspectives that exceed a confidence threshold spawn a mutated child perspective (e.g., altered edge‑threshold or a new glyph dictionary) via MothQuantum‑seeded mutation. The tissue then adopts the child perspective with the highest score, allowing the system to specialise per region and per frame.",
      "jev_role": "Scores each perspective’s local projection and decides whether a child perspective should be created (via a ‘noul‑>yes/no’ query).",
      "hypothesis": "Specialised perspective allocation will increase object‑label fidelity from the low 0.03‑0.24 range observed in E1 to >0.35 on average across frames. Refuted if mean object fidelity ≤0.30 after three growth cycles.",
      "builds_on": "E1 (tissue‑level loss of object information) and E3 (guided growth improves edge fidelity but mixing styles creates seams).",
      "cost": "Initial cost = 6 Jev queries per tissue per growth round (≈ 150 ms each). With 6×4=24 tissues and 2 growth rounds, total ≈ 4.3 minutes of Jev time; mutations are cheap integer operations.",
      "beyond_classic_ml": "Creates a decentralized, evolving ensemble of feature extractors that adapt their parameters locally rather than learning a single monolithic model."
    },
    {
      "name": "Holarchic Meta‑Jury with Quantum Seeding (HMJQS)",
      "levels": ["family", "organism", "community"],
      "mechanism": "Generate N=8 Jury configurations by seeding different random seeds with MothQuantum (each config varies number of VLM critics, weighting scheme, and whether a Jev‑judge is used). For a given frame, a top‑level Jev meta‑critic asks a choice question over which Jury configuration is most likely to succeed, based on a quick heuristic (e.g., edge density, motion variance). The selected Jury then runs its full critic aggregation to produce the final projection. The meta‑jury itself is re‑seeded each epoch.",
      "jev_role": "Acts as the meta‑critic that selects the best Jury configuration; also scores the final projection for feedback.",
      "hypothesis": "HMJQS will achieve a fidelity of ≥0.42 on edge‑glyph text, surpassing the best static Jury result of 0.354 (E2) and the oracle ceiling of 0.433. Refuted if the measured fidelity is ≤0.38.",
      "builds_on": "E2 (community jury outperforms averaging) and the principle that consensus helps when agents are competent; adds a higher‑level selection layer.",
      "cost": "One Jev meta‑question per frame + up to 6 VLM critic calls for the selected Jury (average 3 critics per Jury). Total ≈ 2–3 VLM calls per frame, similar to baseline experiments, plus negligible quantum seed generation.",
      "beyond_classic_ml": "Introduces a hierarchical ensemble where not only individual models vote but entire voting schemas are selected dynamically, a level of meta‑learning absent in conventional ensemble methods."
    }
  ]
}

You are one member of a research community with no central editor. Here is what the community measured, and every idea proposed in the first round (by you and your peers).

MEASURED RESULTS (ground truth, bootstrap 95% CIs) from experiments built out of the community's first ideas:
E1 holarchic reader: tissues (6x3 tiles) of a character-art frame answer first-person typed questions (TypeSafe Jev), fuse into organs by a local rule, no VLM. Fidelity vs truth: 0.30 on brightness-only text (a VLM reading the same text: 0.28), about 60% of the VLM on edge-glyph text (VLM 0.49-0.51 vs swarm 0.24-0.31). Tissues recognise background well (0.87-1.0) but what object they hold poorly (0.03-0.24): information dies at tissue-level 'what', not at organ assembly. Motion arrows survive (motion recall 0.40). Letting tissues hear neighbours' claims spread object labels into empty sky: background accuracy 0.87 -> 0.63, net fidelity down (not significant).
E2 community jury: three VLM critics reconstruct the same text. Believing the reconstruction the other two agree with most (no judge, no centre) beats averaging them: 0.354 vs 0.301 (+0.053, CI [0.016, 0.089]); a Jev judge choosing among them +0.042 (CI [0.006, 0.078]); oracle 0.433.
E3 guided growth: 8x4 tissues sense their patch of the real frame as numbers and choose how to draw themselves (tone / edges / braille / motion arrows); a second round hearing neighbours' CHOICES helps (+0.066, CI [0.002, 0.128]) but the mosaic only ties drawing everything with edges (0.328 vs 0.350, n.s.): mixing styles creates seams. Jev almost never chose the motion style (6 of 320 tissues).
E4 kaleidoscope: each tissue has two independent weak senses (raw text, numeric receptors). Asserting an object only where both agree collapses fidelity to 0.10 (they rarely agree); their UNION beats the better sense (+0.046, CI [0.019, 0.076]) and ties an oracle that knows which sense to trust.
PRINCIPLE (provisional): consensus helps when members are individually competent and errors are noise; union helps when members are weak and err in different places; gossiping BELIEFS spreads errors, gossiping CHOICES coordinates.
